findings.claim: D9's registration probe `claude mcp get gabe-map` is not a read — the CLI health-checks approved servers by launching them, so once gabe-map is registered every `./install.sh` (and every doctor run, per §7's INFO line) spawns `python3 ~/.claude/skills/gabe-map/scripts/server.py`, and a broken-but-registered server reports as NOT REGISTERED.
findings.failure_scenario: Operator registers gabe-map, later edits server.py and introduces a startup traceback, then runs `./install.sh`. The probe `claude mcp get gabe-map` spawns the server, the handshake fails, the probe exits non-zero, and install prints `NOT registered — ./install.sh --register-mcp`. The operator re-runs registration; `~/.claude.json` already holds the entry, nothing changes, and the actual defect (a broken server.py) is never named. Second scenario: install.sh runs `set -e` (install.sh:9) and `run(){ eval "$@" }` (install.sh:21-27); a bare `run "claude mcp get gabe-map"` aborts the whole install
findings.evidence: `claude mcp --help` (2.1.257): `get <name>` — "approved servers are health-checked"; `claude mcp list --help` — "approved servers are health-checked unless disabled for this project". findings.fix: Drop `claude mcp get` as the probe. Read `~/.claude.json` with python3 stdlib: `mcpServers["gabe-map"]` for presence, `projects[<abs cwd>].disabledMcpServers` for per-project suppression (that key is real and populated — `/home/khujta/projects/gabe_lens` carries `["magic","pencil"]`). A pure JSON read spawns nothing, cannot false-negative on a broken server, and is the only way to answer the per-project half of the question §2 says `map_status` must answer.

findings.claim: tests/gabe-map/run.sh is the first battery to drive a long-lived bidirectional subprocess, and suite-doctor runs every battery with NO timeout — a blocked client read hangs the doctor forever instead of failing it.
findings.failure_scenario: Per §5, `notifications/initialized` makes the server send `{"id":"srv-1","method":"roots/list"}` and (per D4) wait for the reply. The documented 2–4 min doctor budget becomes unbounded, with no failing exit code and no partial output (the subshell buffers everything).
findings.evidence: scripts/suite-doctor.sh:98-112 — the loop is `_out=$(bash "$h" 2>&1); _rc=$?` with no `timeout` wrapper anywhere in the script; the only opt-out is the by-name `scope-prompt-harness` skip at :103. Every other `tests/*/run.sh` is pure python/bash with no persistent child.
findings.fix: In client.py give every read a deadline (non-blocking `select` on the pipe, hard fail after ~5 s per message); in run.sh wrap each client invocation in `timeout 30` and add `trap 'kill $SRV_PID 2>/dev/null' EXIT`. findings.claim: The `SERVER_OVERRIDE`/`MQ_OVERRIDE` hooks inherit a trap already present in reach-emit: an out-of-tree mutant cannot find its sibling scripts, so it emits 0 for the wrong reason and every mutant 'fails an assert' vacuously.
findings.failure_scenario: Measured: copying reach-emit.py to the scratchpad and running `RE_OVERRIDE=<copy> bash tests/reach-emit/run.sh` fails 5 asserts with 0 deltas (12/17) — `_MAP_DELTAS` is `dirname(__file__)/../../gabe-commit/scripts/map-deltas.py`. mapquery will have four such siblings (gabe-commit, gabe-cc-entity, gabe-pulse, server→mapquery). A `dedupe-off` or `prose-emitted` mutant placed in a temp dir fails the FIRE assert because the writer was never found, not because the mutation was caught — non-evidence (meta-review P2).
findings.evidence: Shell run this session: `reach-emit battery: 12 passed, 5 failed` under an out-of-tree RE_OVERRIDE vs 17/17 baseline; skills/gabe-red/scripts/reach-emit.py:33-34; design-draft.md:213, 232-233.
findings.fix: State the mutant placement rule in §8: mutants are same-dir temp files (`mapquery.mut.py`, removed in the battery's `trap`), or mapquery resolves siblings via `GABE_SKILLS_DIR` (default `dirname(__file__)/../..`) which the battery sets. First assert of the mutation run: the UN-mutated override passes FIRE, so a later failure is attributable to the mutation.

findings.claim: D4 promises a `root` outside the session's roots is read-only, but the D6 gate list never checks it and the writer runs with `cwd=<root>`.
findings.failure_scenario: From the suite session, `who_calls(apply_recipe_filters, root="/home/khujta/projects/apps/gustify")` → `.kdbp/` exists there → `map-deltas.py append` writes gustify's `.kdbp/map-deltas.jsonl` from another project's session (and, per finding 3, untracked in a tracked dir).
findings.evidence: design-draft.md:44-46 (read-only promise) vs :52-66 (gates a–c only); skills/gabe-commit/scripts/map-deltas.py:41-47, 73-81 (writes under whatever toplevel cwd resolves to).
findings.fix: Gate (e): emit only when `root` ∈ {`CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR`, `roots[]`}; otherwise `emit_skipped: "root outside session roots (read-only)"`. One battery case with an explicit foreign root → 0 lines.

findings.claim: reach-emit's per-symbol CAP note and dry-run lines are `print`ed, and its writer child inherits fd 1 — neither fits a core that must have no stdout when fd 1 is the JSON-RPC wire.
findings.failure_scenario: `process()` prints `note: … capped` (reach-emit.py:96-98) and `_emit` prints `DELTA …` under `--dry-run` (:80-82); `redirect_stdout(sys.stderr)` catches Python prints but NOT the child `subprocess.run([… map-deltas.py append …], cwd=repo)` (:83-86) which inherits the wire — any future stdout from the writer (a warning, a print) corrupts a frame. A >20-file delta also loses its 'capped' notice silently in `who_calls` unless the note is returned.
findings.evidence: skills/gabe-red/scripts/reach-emit.py:78-99; design-draft.md:38-40 (mapquery 'no stdout'), :174-176.
findings.fix: Core returns `notes[]` and `capped:bool` (reach-emit prints them; the server puts them in `structuredContent`); every child process gets `stdout=subprocess.DEVNULL` or `PIPE`. Battery: fixture with 21 grep-only files → `capped:true`, 20 lines.

findings.claim: 'callers arm returned ≥1 match' is ambiguous between symbol-resolved-with-zero-hits and unresolved, and the battery only covers the unresolved case.
findings.failure_scenario: Measured on gustify: unknown symbol → rc 1, stdout empty, stderr `✗ no symbol "…" in the graph — check spelling or run graft build` (a directive-shaped string that must never be echoed); a resolved symbol returns `matches:[{symbol:{…}, hits:[…]}]` and a resolved-but-uncalled one returns `hits:[]`. Under the literal text, a builder could treat `hits:[]` as 'no match' and suppress legit `_a3_graft.calls` deltas for a symbol graft indexed but whose call edges it missed — the clearest recall-gap signal the loop has.
findings.evidence: Shell probe: `graft callers zzz… --json --no-refresh` rc=1, stdout 0 bytes, stderr 88 bytes; `graft callers _rows` → two matches (alembic + account_export) with 1 hit each; design-draft.md:56-58, 226-227.
findings.fix: Define match = `matches[]` non-empty (symbol resolved), hits may be empty; add the resolved-zero-hits fixture (expect emits for code-shaped grep-only files) next to `matches: []` (expect 0); assert graft's stderr text never appears in any result field.

findings.claim: Claude Code feeds the model the serialized structuredContent and DROPS every text content block whenever structuredContent is present, so the design's compact human text (and the D5 honest-empty guidance carried in it) never reaches the model and the 25k budget is spent on the JSON, not the ≤2k-token text.
findings.failure_scenario: `map_status` on a no-center root returns content:[text:'no command center under <root> … Grep/Glob are the source of truth here. Build one: /gabe-cc-init.'] + structuredContent:{present:false,…} → the model receives only `{"present":false,…}`; the guidance/nudge text is gone. `entity_context detail:"full"` returns a small text + the full JSON pack → the JSON is what is measured against MAX_MCP_OUTPUT_TOKENS (25000) and, above the threshold, is persisted to disk and replaced by a file reference — the '≤ ~2k tokens typical' sizing describes a payload the model never gets.
findings.evidence: Claude Code 2.1.258 bundle, MCP result→model converter: `if("structuredContent"in e&&e.structuredContent!==void 0){let h=b(e.structuredContent)…if("content"in e&&Array.isArray(e.content)){let w=e.content.filter((v)=>…v.type!=="text");…}return{content:h,type:"structuredContent",schema:y}}` (text blocks filtered out; only non-text blocks survive alongside the JSON). Cap: `var C=0.5,l=1600,d=25000;function c(){let e=a.MAX_MCP_OUTPUT_TOKENS;…return d}`. Design §5 L187-188 and D5 L47-48 assume both channels are delivered.
findings.fix: Pick ONE channel: v1 returns content:[{type:'text'}] only (the model sees exactly the rendering the design sized), OR keep structuredContent and move every human-facing string (D5 honest-empty guidance, D7 nudge, `reach_line`, freshness stamp, `+N more (cap 40)` notes, `floors[]`) INTO the JSON and size the JSON. Either way make tests/gabe-map/client.py assert on what the model gets (json.dumps(structuredContent) size when present), not on content[0].text.

findings.claim: contextlib.redirect_stdout(sys.stderr) only rebinds Python's sys.stdout; child processes inherit the real fd 1 (the MCP wire), and the emit path the server is refactored onto spawns map-deltas.py with inherited stdio.
findings.failure_scenario: reach-emit._emit → subprocess.run([python, map-deltas.py, 'append', …], cwd=repo) with no stdout capture; any child stdout (a future confirmation print in append, a graft banner if capture is dropped, a shell echo) lands on the wire. A stray write WITHOUT a trailing newline glues onto the server's next JSON frame → the client's ReadBuffer fails JSON.parse on that line and skips it → the tools/call response is lost and the call hangs until the tool timeout. A clean stray line is silently dropped by the client but a valid-JSON non-RPC line raises onerror.
findings.evidence: Demo this session: `with redirect_stdout(sys.stderr): subprocess.run([sys.executable,'-c','print(...)'])` → child output appeared on fd 1 (`python3 fd1demo.py 2>/dev/null` printed 'CHILD PRINT -> inherits fd 1'). reach-emit.py:83-86 (`subprocess.run([...map-deltas.py append...], cwd=repo)` — no capture). Bundle ReadBuffer: `this._buffer=this._buffer.subarray(e+1);try{return _Dt(t)}catch(r){if(r instanceof SyntaxError)continue;throw r}` (bad line consumed+skipped). Spec 2025-11-25 transports: 'The server MUST NOT write anything to its stdout that is not a valid MCP message.'
findings.fix: At server start: `wire=os.dup(1); os.dup2(2,1)` so fd 1 IS stderr for everything (Python prints, C-level writes, children); write frames only through `os.fdopen(wire,'wb',buffering=0)` with a full-write loop + no interleaving; drop redirect_stdout; still pass stdout=DEVNULL/PIPE to every child. Read stdin via sys.stdin.buffer.readline() decoded errors='replace' (a stray invalid UTF-8 byte must not kill the loop). Battery mutant: a fake `graft` that prints a banner without newline → every response still arrives.

findings.claim: `--allowedTools "mcp__gabe-map__.*"` is a permission GLOB, not a regex: `.*` requires a literal dot, matches no tool, and auto-approves nothing; the cited 'probe exit 0' cannot detect this because a denied tool call still exits 0 in -p mode.
findings.failure_scenario: `GABE_MAP_E2E=1 bash tests/gabe-map/run.sh` → `claude -p … --allowedTools "mcp__gabe-map__.*"` → the model's `mcp__gabe-map__map_status` call is denied (no interactive prompt in -p), the model reports it could not call the tool, exit 0; the §8 assertion 'the model called map_status' fails or, if asserted on exit code, passes falsely.
findings.evidence: code.claude.com/docs/en/permissions: 'Allow rules accept tool-name globs only after a literal mcp__<server>__ prefix … `mcp__puppeteer__*` matches every tool from the puppeteer server'; `mcp__puppeteer` (bare) matches all tools. The `.*` form is hook-MATCHER regex syntax (docs/en/hooks 'mcp__<server>__.*'), not permission syntax. Design §2 row 8 and §8 L236-237.
findings.fix: Use `--allowedTools mcp__gabe-map` (or `"mcp__gabe-map__*"`); assert the tool_use via `--output-format stream-json` (a `tool_use` block named mcp__gabe-map__map_status), never on exit code; correct §2 row 8's evidence.

findings.claim: CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR is the directory the session started in, not the git toplevel; running `git grep` with cwd=<root> from a subdirectory restricts the search to that subtree and prints cwd-relative paths, breaking the grep arm's recall, the delta path keys, and the `.kdbp` gate.
findings.failure_scenario: Session launched from gustify/apps/api → root=…/apps/api; center found by walk-up at the toplevel, but `who_calls(list_recipes)`: (i) grep arm never sees apps/web callers; (ii) found/pointer = `services/recipes.py:38` instead of `apps/api/services/recipes.py:38` → the ledger key (gen,subject,file) differs from red's reach-emit key for the SAME edge, splitting the S14 tally; (iii) `<root>/.kdbp` does not exist (it is at the toplevel) → the server emits 0 while map-deltas.py (which resolves .kdbp via `git rev-parse --show-toplevel`) would have written.
findings.evidence: docs/en/hooks: '`${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR}`: the project root where the session started' (worktree note: cwd moves, CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR stays). Demo: from skills/gabe-red, `git grep -nwI -e _noise -- '*.py'` printed `scripts/reach-emit.py:38…` (subtree-restricted, cwd-relative); `--full-name` + `:/*.py` printed `skills/gabe-red/scripts/reach-emit.py:38…`. map-deltas.py:41-55 (`_git_root` → toplevel; `_kdbp(root)`). Design D4 L42-44, D12 L87-91, D6 L55.
findings.fix: Normalize root := `git -C <root> rev-parse --show-toplevel` when it succeeds (else the dir containing the center walk-up hit); run `git grep --full-name … -- ':/*.py' ':/*.ts' …` from the toplevel; report `root` as the toplevel; battery case: CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR=<fixture>/sub resolves the fixture toplevel and emits toplevel-relative paths.

findings.claim: `git grep` exits 1 on no match and 128 when not in a git repo, and `graft callers` exits 1 for an un-indexed symbol vs FileNotFoundError when the binary is absent; the reused `_run` collapses every non-zero rc to None, so 'arm unavailable' is reported as a clean zero.
findings.failure_scenario: `--mcp-config` from a non-git dir (or CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR at an un-git'd copy): grep arm rc=128 → grep{code_files:[]}, missed_by_map:[] → who_calls answers 'no callers' with no signal that the arm did not run — the exact trap the design's own `floors[]` string warns about. Same for graft: binary missing, index broken, and symbol-not-indexed all render as `map_claim:"absent"`.
findings.evidence: Probes: `git grep … zzz` rc=1; `cd /tmp && git grep …` rc=128 'fatal: not a git repository'; `graft callers zzz_nope_zzz . --json --no-refresh` rc=1, stdout empty, stderr '✗ no symbol "zzz_nope_zzz" in the graph — check spelling or run graft build'. reach-emit.py:43-48 (`return r.stdout if r.returncode == 0 else None`). Design D5 L49 ('Unknown symbol in graft → map_claim: absent (not indexed)') and D12 L87-90 give no not-a-repo path.
findings.fix: In mapquery.two_arm return per-arm status: grep rc 0/1 → ran (matches/none), rc ≥2 or OSError → `grep_arm:{status:'unavailable', reason:<stderr first line>}`; graft rc 1 + 'no symbol' → `absent (not indexed)`, FileNotFoundError → `unavailable (graft not on PATH)`, other → `unavailable (<stderr>)`. Battery: a non-git root → who_calls carries status 'unavailable' and emits nothing.

findings.claim: map-deltas.py append returns 0 both when it wrote a line and when it silently no-op'd (no .kdbp at the git toplevel), so `deltas_emitted:n` can only count attempts, not writes.
findings.failure_scenario: Root is a subdir (see root-not-toplevel) or .kdbp is missing at the toplevel while the server's own `<root>/.kdbp` check passed → the server reports `deltas_emitted:1` and `reach_line` implies a recorded delta, but .kdbp/map-deltas.jsonl gained nothing; the dedupe gate (c) reading `<root>/.kdbp/map-deltas.jsonl` and the writer's `<toplevel>/.kdbp/` can also point at different files.
findings.evidence: map-deltas.py:73-76 (`if not kd: return 0  # not a KDBP project — silent no-op`) and :80-82 (write path also returns 0); design §4.4 L148 `deltas_emitted:n`, D6 L55 'ONLY when .kdbp/ exists'.
findings.fix: Import map-deltas.py via spec_from_file_location and call `append()` in-process (still the one validated writer) using the SAME `_git_root()/_kdbp()` resolution for the gate and the dedupe read, and count only calls that actually wrote (check `os.path.getsize` before/after, or extend append to return a distinct code for no-op).

findings.claim: Claude Code 2.1.258 ships the dual-era MCP client: in `MCP_PROTOCOL_NEGOTIATION=auto` (default today is `legacy`) the FIRST frame is a `server/discover` request with a string id before any `initialize`; the design's pre-init rule works by accident (-32602 is 'a non-modern error') but uses the wrong code for an unknown method and has no battery case, and a server that closes on a pre-init unknown method fails negotiation outright.
findings.failure_scenario: Operator or a future default flips negotiation to `auto` → client sends `{"id":"server-discover-probe-1","method":"server/discover"}` pre-init. A build that (a) answers with id null/int-coerced, (b) exits on a pre-init protocol violation, or (c) answers -32022 → 'treating the server as pre-2026-07-28' fallback is skipped or 'Version negotiation failed: the transport was closed during the server/discover probe' → gabe-map never connects in any project.
findings.evidence: Bundle strings: 'server/discover probe reply did not echo the request id (expected …) — treating the server as pre-2026-07-28', 'Version negotiation failed: the transport was closed during the server/discover probe', probe id `server-discover-probe-${++this._probeCounter}`, env `MCP_PROTOCOL_NEGOTIATION` ('expected legacy or auto'), SDK default `var ol="legacy"`. Spec 2026-07-28 versioning: stdio clients 'probe with server/discover and fall back on any error that is not a recognized modern error' (modern = -32022 UnsupportedProtocolVersionError). Design §5 L182 ('Pre-initialize requests other
findings.fix: Pre-init unknown method → -32601 with the request id echoed verbatim (preserve string ids), never -32022, never close/exit; add a battery case: `server/discover` before initialize → error code ∉ {-32022} with the same string id, then `initialize` still succeeds; document `MCP_PROTOCOL_NEGOTIATION` in map-spec.

findings.claim: On an unsupported requested protocolVersion the server answers 2025-06-18 although it supports 2025-11-25; the spec says the fallback SHOULD be the server's latest, and the battery pins the SHOULD-violation.
findings.failure_scenario: A future client whose supported list has dropped 2025-06-18 but still lists 2025-11-25 sends a newer version string → server answers 2025-06-18 → client `if(!r.includes(a.protocolVersion)) throw "Server's protocol version is not supported"` → connection refused, though the server actually speaks a version the client accepts.
findings.evidence: Spec 2025-11-25 lifecycle: 'Otherwise, the server MUST respond with another protocol version it supports. This SHOULD be the latest version supported by the server.' Bundle client check: `if(!r.includes(a.protocolVersion))throw Error("Server's protocol version is not supported: …")`. Design §2 row 1 L21 and §8 L214-215 ('garbage version → 2025-06-18').
findings.fix: Supported set = {2025-11-25, 2025-06-18}; echo the request when in the set, else answer 2025-11-25; update the battery assert accordingly.

findings.claim: `roots/list` results carry file:// URIs (percent-encoded) and may be an error response (-32601 when the client lacks roots); the design treats `roots[0]` as a path and its 'id no method → a response' branch names only results, and it does not say tool calls must not block on the roots reply.
findings.failure_scenario: CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR unset and a project at `/home/u/My Project` → roots uri `file:///home/u/My%20Project` → isdir False → fallback to os.getcwd() (= ~/.claude at user scope) → false honest-empty 'no command center'. A client error reply to srv-1 that isn't handled → the pending-roots state never resolves.
findings.evidence: Spec 2025-11-25 roots: 'uri … MUST be a file:// URI'; error handling: 'Client does not support roots: -32601'. Design D4 L42-43 ('roots[0] … matched by a srv-N id'), §5 L178.
findings.fix: Decode with `urllib.parse.unquote(urlparse(uri).path)`; accept `error` responses for srv-N ids; never block a tools/call on the roots reply (root resolution reads whatever has arrived).

findings.claim: Hooks DO fire for MCP tools (PreToolUse/PostToolUse with matcher `mcp__<server>__.*` and tool_input = the arguments); the 'HOOK-VISIBILITY COLLISION' exists only because the KDBP hook matchers are `Write|Edit|MultiEdit` and `Bash`, so Q2's 'never, or design a hook-visible write path first' premise is off — the path exists.
findings.failure_scenario: The operator rules 'never' on mutation tools based on a stated impossibility that is not one; conversely, the D6 delta emit is presented as guarded by no hook when a PostToolUse on `mcp__gabe-map__who_calls` could observe it today.
findings.evidence: docs/en/hooks: 'MCP server tools appear as regular tools in tool events (PreToolUse, PostToolUse, PostToolUseFailure, PermissionRequest, PermissionDenied)… mcp__<server>__.* (the .* is required)'; templates/hooks.json matchers: PLAN-PROOF-GUARD `Write|Edit|MultiEdit`, KDBP CHECKPOINT/PUSH-GATE-GUARD `Bash`. Design D14 L96-98, §11 Q2 L259-260.
findings.fix: Reword D14: 'the KDBP hooks' matchers do not include mcp__gabe-map__.*; a mutation tool would need the matcher extended (`Write|Edit|MultiEdit|mcp__gabe-map__.*`) and tool_input-based path checks' — no v1 change.

findings.claim: Three §2 rows cite 'docs' for claims the current docs do not make, and the wire's 10 MiB per-frame cap is unnamed.
findings.failure_scenario: A reader trusts the table: (a) 'Restart required after claude mcp add — docs' — the MCP page has no such statement (only /reload-plugins for plugin servers); (b) 'docs: user-scope cwd = ~/.claude' — the table with that cwd is for `headersHelper`, not the server process; (c) the env-vars page says MAX_MCP_OUTPUT_TOKENS default 8000 while the bundle uses 25000 — a builder reading env-vars sizes to 8k and mis-reports the cap name; (d) a result frame >10 MiB clears the client ReadBuffer and the response is lost (no design law forbids it beyond D11's soft caps).
findings.evidence: code.claude.com/docs/en/mcp (no restart statement; headersHelper cwd table); docs/en/env-vars MAX_MCP_OUTPUT_TOKENS 'default: 8000' vs bundle `d=25000`; bundle `var za=10485760 … ReadBuffer exceeded maximum size of ${this._maxBufferSize} bytes` with `this.clear()`. Design §2 rows L24, L26, L27.
findings.fix: Re-cite rows 24/27 as 'probe' or drop 'docs'; state 'cap 25k (bundle-verified; env-vars page stale)'; add a map-spec wire law: one frame ≤ 1 MiB (well under the client's 10 MiB ReadBuffer) enforced by projection, with a battery assert on the largest fixture result.
